executive_summary: In highlight coverage, our World Cup prediction market analysis dominated earned media this week, with TradingView, BeInCrypto, and incrypted reporting our $20B blockchain volume finding across English, Korean, and French outlets. We also secured significant thought leadership placement on stablecoin infrastructure maturation ($1.5 quadrillion annual processing potential by 2035 via CoinMarketCap) and critical security research on the Coldcard exploit ($30M stolen targeting high-value wallets, covered by CryptoRank and Bitcoin World). Our Polymarket partnership announcement for insider trading detection tools appeared on quasa.io, positioning us as compliance infrastructure leaders. In crypto news, the Coldcard self-custody security crisis accelerated institutional migration toward Bitcoin ETFs (CoinDesk), while Tether reported $1.5B Q2 operating profit amid stablecoin maturation narratives, and the SEC moved to review Nasdaq bitcoin options after CME challenges (CoinDesk). In competitor news, Elliptic secured three enterprise wins (Sei, HashKey, unnamed exchange with $3.1M efficiency gains) positioning themselves as enterprise compliance infrastructure; Arkham pivoted to full decentralization on their exchange; and TRM Labs gained visibility through AI-scam fighting commentary by Ari Redbord.

market_landscape.title: Institutional Adoption Accelerates Via Security Concerns
market_landscape.body: Self-custody crisis (Coldcard $30M+ exploit) is pushing retail and mid-market investors toward regulated Bitcoin ETFs and institutional custody, validating TradFi-crypto convergence thesis and creating immediate demand for institutional-grade compliance tooling.

market_landscape.title: Stablecoin Payment Infrastructure Nears Critical Mass
market_landscape.body: Projection of $1.5 quadrillion annual processing by 2035, Tether's $1.5B Q2 profit, and World Cup prediction market volumes demonstrate payment layer maturation; regulatory scrutiny (EU sanctions packages, Bank of Italy efficiency questions) signals inflection point between speculative and productive use cases.

market_landscape.title: AI-Enhanced Threats Reshape Compliance Automation
market_landscape.body: AI-driven scam sophistication and ransomware targeting intelligence is outpacing traditional rule-based detection; competitor TRM Labs gaining traction on AI-scam fighting, while our hybrid blockchain and institutional surveillance positioning provides differentiation but requires visible AI-native narrative.

competitor_reads.Elliptic: Positioned as enterprise compliance infrastructure leader with three major wins (Sei, HashKey, unnamed $3.1M efficiency exchange) and stablecoin compliance thought leadership; gaining traction in regulated VASP space.
competitor_reads.TRM Labs: Gaining visibility on AI-scam fighting expertise (Ari Redbord commentary); positioned as specialized threat detection player but with narrow public profile compared to our broader institutional footprint.
competitor_reads.Arkham Intelligence: Pivoting exchange to full decentralization and driving speculation engagement via on-chain data tokenization; lacks compliance-focused positioning versus our institutional risk management narrative.
competitor_reads.Merkle Science: Positioning as privacy-preserving blockchain analytics (regulatory-friendly privacy), occupying niche between us and pure privacy advocates; limited earned media but targeting compliance-conscious institutions.
